title: Product [[0,1]]×X of a finite-mass current: existence, uniqueness, mass, support, slice continuity, normality and the boundary formula (Simon 2.17–2.22; supplied 3.1–3.4)
statement: Notation: for s ∈ ℝ and x ∈ ℝ^m, cons(s, x) := (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin (m+1)) ℝ).symm (Fin.cons s (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin m) ℝ x)) ∈ ℝ^{m+1}; ι(v) := cons(0, v); e₀ := EuclideanSpace.single 0 1 ∈ ℝ^{m+1}; for y ∈ ℝ^{m+1}, t(y) := EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin (m+1)) ℝ y 0 and tl(y) := (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin m) ℝ).symm (Fin.tail (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin (m+1)) ℝ y)); cyl(A) := {y : t(y) ∈ [0,1], tl(y) ∈ A}. D_q(ℝ^p) := GeometricCurrentOn univ q, D^q(ℝ^p) := TestFormOn univ q, M = mass, spt = support, ∂ = boundary. For X ∈ D_k(ℝ^m) and Z ∈ D_{k+1}(ℝ^{m+1}), ProdChar(X, Z) means: for every η ∈ D^{k+1}(ℝ^{m+1}) and every φ : ℝ → D^k(ℝ^m) with φ(s)(x)(v_1, …, v_k) = η(cons(s, x))(e₀, ι(v_1), …, ι(v_k)) for all s ∈ [0,1], x ∈ ℝ^m, v ∈ (ℝ^m)^k (Fin.cons e₀ (ι ∘ v)), one has Z(η) = ∫_0^1 X(φ(s)) ds (interval integral). (I) For all m, k ∈ ℕ and X ∈ D_k(ℝ^m) with M(X) < ∞ there is Z ∈ D_{k+1}(ℝ^{m+1}) such that: ProdChar(X, Z); every Z′ ∈ D_{k+1}(ℝ^{m+1}) with ProdChar(X, Z′) equals Z; M(Z) ≤ M(X); spt Z ⊆ cyl(spt X); for every η and φ as in ProdChar the map s ↦ X(φ(s)) is continuous on [0,1]; and, if for every j ∈ ℕ and Y ∈ D_{j+1}(ℝ^m) with k = j + 1 and HEq Y X one has M(∂Y) < ∞, then M(∂Z) < ∞. (II) For all m, every X ∈ D_0(ℝ^m) with M(X) < ∞, every Z ∈ D_{0+1}(ℝ^{m+1}) with ProdChar(X, Z), every ψ ∈ D^0(ℝ^{m+1}) and all ψ₀, ψ₁ ∈ D^0(ℝ^m) with ψ_i(x)(v) = ψ(cons(i, x))(ι ∘ v) for all x, v (i = 0, 1): ∂Z(ψ) = X(ψ₁) − X(ψ₀). (III) For all m, j, every X ∈ D_{j+1}(ℝ^m) with M(X) < ∞, every Z ∈ D_{j+1+1}(ℝ^{m+1}) with ProdChar(X, Z), every ψ ∈ D^{j+1}(ℝ^{m+1}), all ψ₀, ψ₁ ∈ D^{j+1}(ℝ^m) with ψ_i(x)(v) = ψ(cons(i, x))(ι(v_1), …, ι(v_{j+1})) for all x, v (i = 0, 1), and every φ : ℝ → D^j(ℝ^m) with φ(s)(x)(v) = ψ(cons(s, x))(e₀, ι(v_1), …, ι(v_j)) for s ∈ [0,1]: ∂Z(ψ) = X(ψ₁) − X(ψ₀) − ∫_0^1 ∂X(φ(s)) ds.
